dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Denise. What's going on?

Hi, yes, um. Hi. My name is Ileana Morales, I'm at 688 Thames Street, down past the Fifth Ward end, and, well, I'm calling because somebody from my house already reported this yesterday and nothing's happened. So I'm calling again.
Okay. You're a little faint, are you on speaker?
I am, sorry, I'm at the desk at the rectory, I do the office work over here at the church a few evenings, and I've got a pile of envelopes in one hand. Is that better? Can you hear me?
That's better. Go ahead, 688 Thames.

Okay. So, um. That storm, the one that started as snow Sunday and turned to rain, that ended Monday. Overnight Sunday into Monday the drain on our corner backed up. And I mean it came up out of the street first, okay, I watched it, it was bubbling up out of the grate, it filled the gutter, and then it came into the house. Into the basement. About three inches.
Okay.

And it's a finished basement, it's not, um, it's not a dirt cellar. My camping gear got soaked, the chest freezer was sitting in it. And that drain is still clogged. Right now. Three days later. There's still water sitting at that corner, it's got slush and junk all over the top of it.
Alright, let me find what's already in there. Who called it in yesterday, do you know?

Doug. Doug Gifford. He rents the in-law unit over the garage. He called, um, yesterday morning, I think late morning, because I was on a job and I couldn't, well, I'm a plumber, I couldn't exactly leave somebody's kitchen torn apart. So he called for me.
Got it. Give me a second, I'm pulling it up.
Sure.
[pause] Okay. Yep, here it is. Wednesday, eleven-ish, drain backup at the corner by 688 Thames. Logged by the office.

Okay, so it's in there. Good. So, um, so where's the crew? Because he told me they said somebody would come look and nobody's come. I came home at lunch today, nothing. Nobody. The grate's the same as it was.
So what I'm seeing is the crew's on the schedule for tomorrow. Friday. That's what was set up when he called.
Tomorrow.
Tomorrow, Friday the thirtieth.

Well, okay, see, that's, um. [pause] That's the thing. Nobody told me tomorrow. Doug might've heard Friday, I don't know, but I'm sitting here thinking it was gonna be today, yesterday, something. And it's been since Monday. That's four days with a blocked drain in front of my house, and if it rains again before then, that water goes right back where it went.
I hear you. After that storm we had backups all over the city, so the crews are going down a list, and yours is on it for tomorrow.

Okay, but, um, every year, well, not every year, but, I've been in that house thirty-one years. Thirty-one. And I've watched that corner fill up more than once, okay, and somebody comes, maybe, and pokes at it and leaves. I don't want somebody coming tomorrow, scraping the leaves off the top and calling it done. Because I know drains. That's my job. If it's coming up out of the grate like that, it's not just the top that's the problem.
That's fair. I can put a note right on the work order that the water came up out of the drain and backed into a basement, so they know it's more than a clogged grate.

Yes. Please. Put that. And, um. I want a supervisor to call me. Not, I mean, no offense to you, you're being very nice, but I want somebody who can actually tell me what's going on under that street to call me back.
No offense taken. I'll put in the request for a supervisor callback. What's the best number?
401-555-0103. And that's for Ileana, spell the last name for me?
M-O-R-A-L-E-S. Ileana is I-L-E-A-N-A.
Okay. Ileana Morales, 688 Thames, supervisor callback requested, basement flooding from the street drain, crew scheduled Friday. That sound right?
That's, um, yeah. [crosstalk] sorry, somebody just came in, hold on, Father, one second. [pause] Sorry. Yeah, that's right.
No problem. The supervisors are in during the day, so realistically that call would come during business hours, not tonight.

Well, that's the other thing. I called this line because City Hall's closed, it's six o'clock, and I work all day, so the only time I can even call anybody is when everybody's gone home. That's why it's taken me till now. I'm not trying to bother the storm line with this, but, um, it is a storm problem. It's from the storm.
You're fine. This is exactly what the line's for. Is there water still coming into the house right now?

No, not right now. We got it out, I got a wet vac going Monday, the carpet's, well, the carpet's another story. But the drain's still full, so if it rains, it's gonna do it again. That's my point. Nobody fixed the thing that caused it.
Understood. If it does start backing up again before the crew gets there, call this number right away, day or night, and we'll get somebody out on it as an emergency.
Okay. [line breaks up] ...tomorrow, what time?
Sorry, you cut out. Did you ask what time tomorrow?
Yeah, what time tomorrow?
It's a day shift, so sometime between morning and mid-afternoon. They go in order, I don't see a slot.
So, um, so I just have to hope. Okay. Well, I'll be on a job, but Doug might be around. He'd see them. I just, I want somebody to actually look down in there this time.
I've got it all in the note. And the supervisor request is in.
Okay. Thank you, Denise. Really, um, I'm not mad at you. I'm just tired of looking at that grate.
I get it. Go finish your envelopes, and call back if it fills up again.
I will. Goodnight.
